comment: The test site: the pages every shell's adapter suite and UI tests load, defined once. Tools/testsite/site.py writes them into each suite's own loopback server (Swift, Kotlin) and can serve them itself. A page with a 'title' is an HTML page with that title, a heading saying the same, and 'body' after it; a page with 'content' is that text, as 'type'. A page with 'base64' is those bytes, as 'type', sent as they are: a picture. 'status' is '200 OK' unless given. 'body' and 'content' may be a list of lines. In a title, a header or a body, {query:NAME|DEFAULT} is the request's query value NAME and {cookie:NAME|DEFAULT} its cookie NAME, or DEFAULT when the request has none. Every answer closes the connection and says Cache-Control: no-store, unless the page gives a Cache-Control header of its own. A page with 'only_for' (name:password) answers only to a request that says so (HTTP Basic); every other request for it is answered with 'refused', which asks who is there. A connection that begins as TLS (the site asked for over https) is answered in plain words, 400, and closed: to a browser that is a secure connection that could not be made.

pages.title: Home
pages.note: Where a suite starts. Its link leads to /landed.

pages.title: Set
pages.note: Signs in: remembers ?v= in a cookie.

pages.title: Session
pages.note: Signs in for the session only: a cookie with no expiry, which an engine keeps in memory.

pages.title: who={cookie:who|none}
pages.note: Says, in its title, who the cookie says is signed in.
Redirects to /landed.

pages.title: Push
pages.note: Changes its own address to /pushed without a load.
A service worker that does nothing but exist.

pages.title: Tall
pages.note: Taller than any window, with a field to type in: for scroll and form restoration.

pages.title: Storage
pages.note: Remembers ?v= in localStorage, or says in its title what was remembered.

pages.title: Tracked
pages.note: A page that fetches something of its own: for the request callback.

pages.title: Uses
pages.note: A page whose script may be kept: for the HTTP cache.
May be kept for an hour. A second request for it means the cache did not have it.

pages.title: Slow
pages.note: Answers after three seconds: a load that is still going when a test stops it.

pages.title: Opener
pages.note: Asks for new windows when clicked: a link with a target, and a button that calls window.open. Says in its title what a window it opened told it. Its other link and button ask for windows on addresses that are for the system and not for a browser: a letter to write, a number to ring.

pages.title: Opened
pages.note: What /opener opens. When the page that opened it has a hold on it, says so in its title and tells that page hello. Its button asks for its own window to be closed.

pages.title: Pops
pages.note: Asks for a window by itself as it loads, with nobody clicking, and says in its title whether it got one.

pages.title: Clicks
pages.note: Clicks its own link to a new window as it loads, with nobody clicking.

pages.title: Contact
pages.note: Links for the system, each followed a different way: a letter by a plain link, a number by a button's script, a message by a link that fills a frame.

pages.title: Find
pages.note: One word three times, once with a capital, each in a paragraph of its own: for find on the page.

pages.title: Rings
pages.note: Goes to a number to ring by itself as it loads, with nobody clicking.

content: A line of words.
pages.note: A page that says it is as wide as the device, as pages made for phones do, with one line of text of a known size, and its words in an element as wide as they are: for zoom.

pages.title: Downloads
body: a file that says it is to be saved
a file of a kind nothing shows
a link that says download
a file whose name is a path
a file that says who is signed in
pages.note: Links that each start a download in a different way: for downloads.
Text a browser could show, sent as an attachment with a name.
Sixteen bytes of a kind no engine shows, with no name suggested.

pages.content: This file's name tried to be a path.
pages.note: An attachment whose suggested name has folders in it.
An attachment that says who the cookie says is signed in: a download is fetched as its login set.

pages.title: Asks
body: function say(what) { document.getElementById('said').textContent = what; document.title = what; if (parent !== window) parent.postMessage(what, '*'); }

navigator.geolocation.getCurrentPosition(function () { say('granted location'); }, function (failed) { say(failed.code === 1 ? 'refused location' : 'granted location, no place ' + failed.code); }, { timeout: 4000 });
pages.note: Asks to use the camera, the microphone, both, or the device's location, by a button or at once with ?now=, and says in its title what became of it: 'asking camera', then 'granted camera 1' (with how many tracks it was given, which it stops at once) or 'refused camera NotAllowedError'. In a frame it tells its parent the same. For permission prompts.

pages.title: Asks in a frame
body: <iframe id="frame" allow="camera; microphone; geolocation" width="320" height="240"></iframe>
pages.note: Holds /asks in a frame from another origin (the same server by its other name, localhost), which asks at once and is allowed by the page to: says in its title what the frame said became of it. For who a permission request is reported to be from.

pages.title: Says
body: function tell(what) { document.getElementById('said').textContent = what; document.title = what; if (parent !== window) parent.postMessage(what, '*'); }
if (what === 'alert') { alert('Your basket is empty.'); tell('alert returned'); }
else { var got = prompt('Your name?', 'Ada'); tell(got === null ? 'prompt nothing' : 'prompt ' + got); }
pages.note: Says something (alert), asks yes or no (confirm) or asks for a word (prompt), by a button or at once with ?now=, and says in its title what it got: 'alert returned', 'confirm true', 'prompt Ada', 'prompt nothing'. In a frame it tells its parent the same. With ?hold=yes it asks to keep the person when they leave. For what a page says or asks.

pages.title: Says in a frame
pages.note: Holds /says in a frame from another origin (the same server by its other name, localhost), which asks at once: says in its title what the frame said it got. For who a page's dialog is reported to be from.

pages.title: Staff only
pages.note: Answers only to the name ada and the password lovelace (HTTP Basic, realm Staff); to anyone else, with `refused`. Its picture asks the same.
A picture only for ada.
Sends a load on to /staff at the server's other name (localhost), on the port ?port= says: for where a load is heading when a server asks.

pages.title: Shows a picture
pages.note: Shows /staff-picture from another origin (the same server by its other name, localhost), or with ?from=own from its own, and says in its title what became of it. For a server asking who is there with no load on its way: the tab's own, and one that is not.

pages.title: Links
pages.note: A link in words, a link that is a picture, words that are no link (one of them an element of its own, to press and hold), and a link for the system. For a link's menu, a link the person asks for in a new tab, and words that are selected.

pages.content: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="160" height="80"><rect width="160" height="80" fill="#c60"/></svg>
pages.note: A picture with a name of its own, big enough to press.

pages.content: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="160" height="80"><rect width="160" height="80" fill="#06c"/></svg>
pages.note: A picture at an address that does not say what kind of file it is: only the site's answer does.

pages.title: Pictures
pages.note: A picture, a picture that is a link, a picture whose address does not say what kind of file it is, and words. With ?menu=own the page takes the menu's event for itself, before anything else of the page can hear it: it keeps the engine's menu from opening, and says so in its title. For a picture's menu.

Sends whoever fetches it on to /whose-file at the server's other name (localhost), on the port ?port= says: another site. For what is sent along when a file a person chose to save turns out to be somewhere else.
Sets the cookie ?v= says, and sends whoever fetches it on to /whose-file at the same site: for a cookie a site sets on the way to a file (027).

pages.title: Downloads elsewhere
body: a file that is at another site
pages.note: A link to a file that says who is signed in, at an address that sends on to the server's other name (localhost), on the port ?port= says: a download a page starts, whose file is at another site (027).
What a page names as its film. It is no film: an engine that tries to play it fails, and the page's player still has its address.

pages.title: Media
body: document.getElementById('made').src = URL.createObjectURL(new Blob(['made by the page'], { type: 'video/mp4' }));
pages.note: A player whose film has an address on the site, and one whose film the page made itself (a blob). With ?menu=own the page takes the menu's event for itself, which keeps the engine's menu from opening. For the menu of a film.

pages.title: Words
pages.note: A word to select, a field with words typed in it, a password's field, and another password's field inside a part of the page that is closed to scripts (in #closed). choose(id) selects what is in one of them. With ?menu=own the page takes the menu's event for itself, which keeps the engine's menu from opening. For a search for words that are selected.

pages.title: Upload
body: var named = files.map(function (file) { return file.name + ' (' + file.size + ')'; }).join(', ');
pages.note: A file input for one file and one for several (which says it accepts text). Says in its title what it was given: each file's name and size, and the words of the first; or that the picker was closed with nothing chosen. For uploads.

pages.title: Sign in
pages.note: A sign-in form of the page's own: a field that says it is for a name and one that says it is for a password, as a password manager looks for them. It sends nothing anywhere but to /landed. Once something is in it, its title says the name and how long the password is (never the password). The name's field is called what ?name= says, for a check by hand that wants to tell this form from another. For the system's filling of passwords (032).

pages.title: Choose
pages.note: A list of choices of the page's own (a select). Says in its title what was chosen. An engine shows such a list in a window of its own over the page, which needs the window the page is in: for the web view's hold on its window (032).
A page that names its icon (046): an orange square of 32 pixels, a PNG given in the page itself, so that no server is asked for a picture.
A picture, as a server sends one: a blue square of 32 pixels, a PNG. What /with-served-icon names as its icon.

A page whose icon is at an address of the site (046): a browser that wants it asks the site for /icon.png, with whatever cookies it has for the site. It says how large the icon is, and links to something that is no icon.

Sends whoever asks for it on to an address named after who their cookie says is signed in: /icon-of-ada, or /icon-of-none. There is nothing at either: what the site was asked for says with whose cookies it was asked.
A page whose icon is at /icon-by-cookie (046): what the site is then asked for says with whose cookies an engine fetches a page's icon.
A picture that has moved (046): sends whoever asks for it on to /icon.png at the same site. A fetch that follows a server within the site ends in the picture.
Sends whoever asks for it on to /icon.png at an address that names somebody and a password, on the port ?port= says (046): a fetch that is made as nobody does not follow it.

refused.title: Sign in needed
refused.note: What a page that is only for someone (only_for) answers to anyone else.
